incidents.victim: Country-code TLD registrars (.as American Samoa, .gh Ghana, .sl Sierra Leone)
incidents.vector: Attackers hijacked DNS records for three ccTLD registries, passing domain ownership verification checks to obtain HTTPS certificates for targeted domains including services operated by Google.
incidents.impact: DNS records modified across three national top-level domain spaces; HTTPS certificates issued for attacker-controlled domains; Google and other organizations' services impersonatable via the hijacked certificates.

incidents.victim: IDC Frontier Cloud (Japanese government cloud infrastructure)
incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed against cloud service provider hosting Japanese government workloads; specific entry vector not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Server infrastructure disrupted across IDC Frontier Cloud environment; Japanese government services dependent on the platform impacted.

incidents.victim: Yandex (Russian internet company — cloud, search, and services)
incidents.vector: Third Ukrainian drone strike on Yandex data centers in four days; physical destruction of data center infrastructure used as a cyber-disruption vector.
incidents.impact: Approximately 80 Yandex cloud services disrupted; Cloudflare observed a 50% drop in Russian bot traffic correlated with the strikes; significant degradation to Russia's largest internet platform.

incidents.victim: Oracle Health (legacy Cerner healthcare platform) — 20 million patients
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to Oracle Health's legacy Cerner system environment; breach occurred approximately one year prior to public disclosure.
incidents.impact: Personal health records for approximately 20 million patients compromised; Oracle withheld disclosure for nearly a year; full scope of data types still being assessed.

incidents.victim: FBI (US Federal Bureau of Investigation) — recruitment portal and agent personnel records
incidents.vector: Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability CVE-2026-35273 against the FBI's contractor-managed recruitment portal; FBI's contractor Accenture had failed to apply available patches.
incidents.impact: Personal and professional data of nearly all FBI special agents stolen, including names, unit assignments, medical and psychiatric records, and specialization details; the FBI subsequently terminated Accenture as a contractor. Three ShinyHunters suspects arrested in the Netherlands, United States, and Jordan.

incidents.victim: Global critical infrastructure, government, healthcare, IT, and education organizations (US, SE Asia, Africa, North America)
incidents.attacker: China — state-linked espionage group (Integrity Technology Group contractor)
incidents.vector: Integrity Technology Group, a Beijing-based contractor with documented Chinese government ties, provides attacker-enabling tooling: EBurst password spraying, MicroScan (1,300+ vulnerability scripts), SoftEther VPN persistence, and XSS credential harvesting. Attackers combine automated scanning with hands-on intrusion.
incidents.impact: Confirmed compromise of US government agencies, manufacturing, healthcare, IT, law enforcement, and education targets; campaign active since at least 2021 and ongoing. Joint advisory AA26-281A issued by 11 nations (US CISA/FBI/NSA, UK NCSC, Australia ACSC, and others). UK government previously sanctioned Integrity Technology Group.

incidents.victim: South Korean financial institutions (multiple banks and brokerage firms)
incidents.vector: Attacker used ARTEX, an open-source agentic penetration testing framework incorporating DeepSeek, GLM, and Grok LLMs, to autonomously identify and exploit vulnerabilities across bank and broker networks; conducted sessions resembling legitimate Claude Code API usage to evade detection.
incidents.impact: Confirmed data exfiltration from at least two South Korean banks; loan origination systems, employee workstations, and customer data repositories accessed. Infrastructure traced to 38.244.50[.]120. South Korean authorities launched investigation.

incidents.victim: Taiwan AI policy research organizations
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing lures themed around AI policy events delivered real-time adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing pages to capture credentials and session tokens from targeted researchers.
incidents.impact: Credential and session token theft targeting Taiwan government-affiliated AI research organizations; likely persistent access established to monitor policy positions.

incidents.victim: Open-source developer ecosystem (npm Axios, Mastra AI, Rust arrayref packages and downstream users)
incidents.vector: North Korea-affiliated actors injected malicious code into widely used open-source packages including the npm Axios HTTP client, the Mastra AI orchestration framework, and the Rust arrayref crate; the ChainDrop worm propagated the payload to over 400 dependent packages.
incidents.impact: Cloud credentials, API keys, and environment variables exfiltrated from developer build pipelines across organizations using the compromised packages; 400+ npm packages infected downstream. Packages have been removed from registries but organizations that ran affected versions during the compromise window should treat credentials as compromised.

incidents.victim: Organizations globally running Fortinet firewall and VPN appliances (86,000+ confirmed compromised devices)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware (INC/Lynx and Payload affiliates)
incidents.vector: Ongoing FortiBleed campaign exploiting credential-exposure vulnerabilities in Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL-VPN gateways; compromised credentials are weaponized for initial access, with ransomware delivered in subsequent stages.
incidents.impact: 86,644+ Fortinet devices confirmed compromised across 194 countries; attackers can lock out device owners and disable defenses before deploying INC Lynx or Payload ransomware. Joint FBI/Secret Service advisory issued October 6, 2026; total exposed device count estimated at 400,000+.

incidents.victim: Osaka Metropolitan University
incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed against university IT network; specific entry vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: University IT network encrypted; classes canceled; academic operations disrupted.

incidents.victim: Organizations using Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway (CVE-2026-88779 — third zero-day)
incidents.vector: Third Citrix NetScaler zero-day disclosed (CVE-2026-88779); exploits SAML authentication to achieve denial-of-service and potential authentication bypass; builds on the same attack surface as CVE-2026-88771/88772.
incidents.impact: Dozens of additional organizations across North America and Europe experiencing service disruption and authentication failures; governments and sector regulators in the US and Australia issued separate emergency advisories.

incidents.victim: Water utilities, telecom providers, regional governments, and universities in Spanish and Portuguese-speaking countries
incidents.vector: Warlock ransomware deployed against organizations across Europe, Africa, and Latin America sharing Spanish or Portuguese as an operating language; sector targeting includes critical infrastructure operators.
incidents.impact: Ransomware-encrypted systems across water utility, telecommunications, regional government, and higher education organizations; operations disrupted in multiple countries; Chinese attribution assessed with moderate confidence based on infrastructure and tooling.

incidents.victim: Danish national population register (CPR) — 8.8 million citizens
incidents.vector: Attacker accessed the Danish central population register via a privileged administrative account protected by the password '123456'; no multi-factor authentication was enforced on the account.
incidents.impact: Names, addresses, and social security numbers (CPR numbers) of all 8.8 million Danish citizens — living and deceased — stolen; data suitable for identity fraud and targeted phishing at national scale.

incidents.victim: US Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) — 3 million DoD personnel records
incidents.vector: Unauthorized actors gained access to a DMDC file-sharing server; access persisted undetected for approximately nine months before discovery.
incidents.impact: Personal data of approximately 3 million current and former US military personnel and DoD civilians exposed, including records held by the agency responsible for maintaining Pentagon personnel files.

incidents.victim: ATNS (Air Traffic and Navigation Services) — South Africa air traffic control
incidents.vector: Ransomware-linked malware introduced into ATNS operational technology (OT) network; data was observed being exfiltrated to IP addresses associated with Chinese infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Air traffic control OT systems at Port Elizabeth Airport and Maputo International Airport affected; South Africa issued an RFQ for forensic incident response services on September 18, 2026; full operational and data impact under investigation.

incidents.victim: Government and policy organizations in Taiwan, India, Philippines, and Cambodia
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing emails delivering the Antino backdoor to government and policy organizations across Southeast and East Asia; campaign tracks regional diplomatic and policy developments.
incidents.impact: Persistent backdoor access established within at least four national governments' policy environments; ongoing surveillance capability enabling intelligence collection on regional geopolitical positions.

incidents.victim: Targeted individuals across iPhone, iPad, and Mac platforms (CVE-2026-86950)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — nation-state or commercial spyware vendor likely
incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-86950, an out-of-bounds write in Apple CoreGraphics (CVSS 8.8), weaponized in 'extremely sophisticated' targeted attacks against specific high-value individuals.
incidents.impact: Arbitrary code execution on affected Apple devices; Apple issued emergency patches and CISA added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day; number of victims small but targets likely high-value.

incidents.victim: Organizations globally using Oracle PeopleSoft (higher education, healthcare, technology, agriculture, transport, government)
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters resumed exploitation of CVE-2026-35273 (Oracle PeopleSoft) against organizations that had applied vendor-recommended workarounds but not full patches; web shells deployed on dozens of systems globally.
incidents.impact: Web shells active on dozens of Oracle PeopleSoft systems globally; data theft and extortion threats issued to victims across higher education, healthcare, government, technology, and agriculture sectors.

incidents.victim: Organizations globally using Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway (CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772)
incidents.vector: Two unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, both CVSS 9.5) in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway; exploitation began as early as September 3, 2026 — approximately three weeks before vendor disclosure on September 27.
incidents.impact: Web shells deployed on compromised NetScaler appliances; 50,277+ internet-exposed instances identified; Mandiant confirmed dozens of organizations across government, financial services, technology, education, and legal sectors in North America and Europe compromised. Exploitation by both nation-state and financially motivated actors observed.

incidents.victim: US financial institutions — ATM networks (1,500+ attacks)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — financial fraud (Tren de Aragua, Venezuelan organized crime)
incidents.vector: Tren de Aragua criminal organization deployed ATM jackpotting malware against US bank ATM networks, causing machines to dispense cash to waiting operatives.
incidents.impact: $40.73 million stolen from US financial institutions via 1,500+ ATM jackpotting attacks through August 2025; US Treasury sanctioned the Tren de Aragua financial network on September 30, 2026; group previously designated as a Foreign Terrorist Organization.

incidents.victim: Unnamed organization — Microsoft Azure cloud tenant
incidents.vector: Agentic AI system (JadePuffer) conducted 15.5 hours of autonomous reconnaissance across an Azure tenant before executing a destructive phase that deleted storage accounts, Key Vault secrets, Function Apps, and App Service plans.
incidents.impact: Complete destruction of Azure tenant resources; databases targeted for deletion; no ransom demand — purely destructive. First documented agentic AI-orchestrated destructive cloud attack.

incidents.victim: iRhythm (cardiac monitoring device company) — 360,000 patients
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to iRhythm patient data systems; entry vector not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: 360,000 patient records stolen including cardiac monitoring data and personal health information; breach occurred in June 2026 and disclosed later.

incidents.victim: Financial services organization (unnamed)
incidents.vector: ClickFix social engineering: target tricked by a fake video conferencing application prompt that copied and executed a malicious PowerShell command, delivering GeniexLoader which then installed GeniexRAT for remote access.
incidents.impact: Full GeniexRAT remote access trojan deployed on victim endpoint; exfiltration capabilities established; consistent with North Korea's ongoing campaign targeting the global financial sector.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian government and critical infrastructure entities (employees at organizations in France, US, and Canada)
incidents.vector: ClickFix technique using fake CAPTCHA prompts embedded in compromised Ukrainian government websites; visiting the page presented a fake browser verification check that copied a malicious PowerShell command to the clipboard and instructed the user to paste and run it.
incidents.impact: VBScript execution and credential theft affecting Ukrainian government sector workers and diaspora employees in France, US, and Canada; access to organizational systems for intelligence collection.

incidents.victim: Iraqi critical infrastructure (telecommunications, aviation) and Israeli entities
incidents.vector: Blinder Tunnel campaign: spear-phishing via fake Dubai Airports recruitment lures delivered ShelbyLoader V2; GitHub repository API used as command-and-control channel to evade network detection; custom tunneling malware for persistent access.
incidents.impact: Initial access established within Iraqi telecommunications and aviation sectors; lateral movement capability for long-term intelligence collection; GitHub infrastructure used for C2 has since been taken down; campaign active from November 2025 through at least June 2026.

incidents.victim: Kiteworks (secure file-sharing platform serving federal agencies)
incidents.vector: Federal threat intelligence warning of imminent targeting prompted Kiteworks to proactively shut down all production systems for inspection; during the shutdown, a critical unauthenticated zero-day was discovered in the Advanced Forms module.
incidents.impact: No exploitation confirmed — Kiteworks patched the critical vulnerability during the proactive shutdown before it could be weaponized; production systems restored after patching. Incident highlights the value of credible government threat intelligence sharing.
